claim_text: In the population of the pivotal study (adults aged 22 and older with diabetes, excluding anyone previously diagnosed with more than mild diabetic retinopathy, with a history of macular edema or retinal vascular occlusion, with ocular injections, retinal laser treatment or intraocular surgery other than uncomplicated cataract surgery, with persistent visual impairment, who cannot be imaged or dilated, who are enrolled in another interventional study, or whose condition could confound the results), EyeArt 2.1.0 detects more than mild diabetic retinopathy as an aid to the clinician in primary care and eye care settings, using the Canon CR-2 AF or CR-2 Plus AF camera.
Validated for patients with diabetes of all ages, including children.
Supports prioritisation of diabetic eye disease for patients presenting to the emergency department or admitted to hospital.
The 2026 release, version 3.0, is covered by the same clearance and the same pivotal study.
Works with any colour fundus camera.
Diagnoses diabetic retinopathy and replaces the dilated eye examination.

Detects more than mild diabetic retinopathy in adults aged 22 and older diagnosed with diabetes who have not been previously diagnosed with more than mild diabetic retinopathy, in primary care and eye care settings, using the Canon CR-2 AF or CR-2 Plus AF camera.
Also detects diabetic retinopathy in patients who have already been diagnosed with more than mild diabetic retinopathy, to monitor progression.
Detects more than mild diabetic retinopathy with a sensitivity of at least 96 percent in primary care and eye care settings.
Prioritises chest radiographs with suspected findings for radiologist review in the emergency department.
Version 2.0 improves sensitivity for all thoracic findings compared with version 1.0.
Notifies the stroke team of suspected large vessel occlusion on CT angiography in the emergency department.
Supports reading of screening mammograms for women aged 40 and over.
Detects more than mild diabetic retinopathy in adults aged 22 and over with diabetes using the Topcon NW400.
Notifies the radiologist of suspected intracranial haemorrhage on non-contrast head CT.
Validated in patients of every age and in every hospital setting.
